standards_review.notes: Both subjects (feat(providers): register SSOSessionExpiryPlugin as a core proxy plugin; feat(providers): detect expired SSO session redirect and trigger re-auth) use an allowed type (feat) and allowed scope (providers), imperative mood, under the 100-char subject-max-length per git-workflow.md

sso-session-expiry.plugin.ts (79 lines) and its test (206 lines) meet code-quality.md: explicit return types on createInterceptor/onUpstreamResponse, .js-extensioned imports, import type used for type-only imports, kebab.plugin.ts/*.test.ts naming, one exported class per file (SSOSessionExpiryInterceptor stays internal), functions under 50 lines, JSDoc explaining the why/SOLID rationale, no console.log, no any

Neither .ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md exists in the repo nor was a security ArtifactRef passed, so there is no documented security checklist to adjudicate against (absent standard, not a gap). Manual review of the new plugin found no concrete security defect: it never logs credentials or cookies, only a static reason string plus the already-known targetApiUrl via the existing markAnalyticsAuthInvalid; the synthetic 401 body is a fixed JSON shape with no reflected user input; re-auth is gated on both the upstream redirect signature and the locally-known credential expiresAt, so a spoofed redirect alone cannot trigger it
